messages:
jess: FYI hit a weird streaming bug in the Python SDK. If the client breaks out of an async-for while an auth refresh runs, the last SSE chunk can be delivered twice and the TCP socket sometimes remains open. Repro below.

tim: rough. do you have a tiny repro so we can run it locally?

jess: yup. server sends three SSE events with small sleeps. client uses SDK.stream() wrapper and cancels mid-stream while spawning a background refresh. This triggers the duplicate final event ~30% of runs under uvloop + httpx.

jess: ```py
# sse_server.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()

async def events():
    yield b"event: a\ndata: 1\n\n"
    await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
    yield b"event: b\ndata: 2\n\n"
    await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
    yield b"event: done\ndata: done\n\n"
@app.get('/sse')
async def sse():
    return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type='text/event-stream')
```

jess: client sketch:

```py
# client_repro.py
async with make_sdk(token) as sdk:
    async for chunk in sdk.stream('/sse'):
        if b'2' in chunk:
            # kick off refresh concurrently and then break out of loop
            asyncio.create_task(do_refresh())
            break
```

jess: logs from one failing run: 

"INFO stream: got event b'2'"
"INFO auth: refresh started (background)"
"DEBUG stream: user called aclose()"
"WARN transport: attempted write after closed? wrote event done again"
"DEBUG gc: StreamIterator finalizer running"

lee: sounds like a lifecycle race between explicit aclose/close and our GC-based finalizer. If the iterator gets wrapped (AsyncIterable vs AsyncIterator) we may delay the close until the wrapper is collected which can re-trigger write attempts.

anya: also saw a typing mismatch in helpers: some helpers accept AsyncIterable[bytes] then wrap the iterator in a helper object that proxies __anext__, adding an extra reference cycle. That changes when __del__ runs.

tim: immediate fixes: 1) make finalizer idempotent and never perform network writes (only drop refs). 2) on aclose(), set a private _disposed/_closed flag and null out transport so finalizer becomes a no-op. 3) avoid wrapping iterators unnecessarily; keep return type as AsyncIterator[bytes] where possible.

lee: agree. I can draft a tiny typing/shape PR to stop the wrapper creation. it's low-risk and will tighten semantics.

jess: quick hack I tested: set stream._closed = True in aclose and it prevented the duplicate write reliably. so flagging works.

tim: can you open an SDK issue with the repro server+client, the log excerpt, and a suggested patch? mark P1 since duplicate sends + dangling sockets break a bunch of client apps.

jess: will open issue and include a tox job matrix suggestion (py3.10/3.11 with/without uvloop/httpx) to catch regressions in CI.
